column1: # Exit criterion E5 — hand-checked anime mappings. 62 rows; E5 asks for 50.
# "Anime titles resolve across AniList and TMDB with correct ID mapping for a
#  hand-checked set of 50 titles including tricky cases (long-running shonen,
#  split-cour seasons, films tied to series)."
# Every anilist_id / imdb_id pair below was written from INDEPENDENT KNOWLEDGE of what
# the work is, not by running the matcher and recording its answer. That distinction is
# the whole value of the file: a fixture generated from the code it tests cannot fail.
# HONESTLY, THOUGH: the first run of `verify-anime` against this file failed 4 of 62,
# and all four were errors in THIS FILE rather than in the matcher.
#   - Yu Yu Hakusho and Nichijou had ids recalled wrongly. tt1710308 is Regular Show.
#     Both were corrected only after checking the catalogue's own title and year for
#     the id the matcher produced, which is independent evidence of what that id is.
#   - Re:Zero and Attack on Titan Season 2 were listed as refusals on a false premise:
#     Re:Zero is resolved by a later title form, and IMDb does hold a separate (sparse,
#     undated) record for Attack on Titan Season 2 rather than only the one series.
# Recorded because a fixture whose failures are quietly edited away until it passes is
# worth nothing, and the next person needs to know which rows were revised and why.
# `expect` is what the pipeline must produce:
#   match       - the AniList entry must map to exactly this IMDb id
#   ambiguous   - the matcher must REFUSE; several catalogue entries are equally good
#   claimed     - resolves correctly, but an earlier entry of the same series holds
#                 the mapping (AniList lists seasons separately, IMDb often does not)
#   conflict    - refused because the years disagree by more than the tolerance
# The negative rows are not filler. They are the ones that fail if someone ever
# "improves" the matcher by breaking ties on popularity.
# Verify with:  cargo run -p sinephile-ingest --bin ingest -- verify-anime
